newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Explorers Index slumps another 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Australian Explorers Index slumps another 2 pct.

text.p: Perth stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index dropped sharply for the fourth consecutive week last week as end-of-financial year-sellers became active.
The Explorers index fell 68 points or 2.15 percent, while the All Ordinaries index fell just 0.37 percent.
In the last month the explorers index has been hammered six percent lower by weak gold prices, while the market overall has rallied nearly five percent.

NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.
Eyres Reed analyst Glen Colgan said in a commentary explorers had been put under pressure by end-of-financial year-sellers.
"Despite this, many resource junionrs began to bounce by the week's end as bargain hunters became active," Colgan said.
Mosaic Oil Nl jumped 13 cents to 41 cents after the company gained a 34 percent interest in an exploration permit in the Bass Strait oil and gas field.
Precious Metals Australia Ltd moved six cents higher to 21 cents ahead of the close of its current non-renounceable issue at 15 cents.
Acclaim Exploration NL dropped 1.4 cents to 4.3 cents after it announced drilling results it described as "disappointing" from its Woodies prospect in Western Australia.
Ramsgate Resources NL and Mt Kare partner Carpenter Pacific Resources NL slipped on continued uncertainty over their tenture over the PNG project.
Ramsgate fell 1.5 cents to 6.5 cents and Carpenter fell 1.5 cents to 27 cents.
